x: Jack Goswell has been a member of Belgrave since April 1951---in fact a new boy. During his 13 years with us he has packed into that time more work than most people achieve in a lifetime.

Jack Goswell (as he had notified us a year earlier) did not seek re-election as Walking Hon Secretary. For fifteen years Jack has done great work for our walkers and the Club and we thank him most sincerely for all his efforts.
…spite making tea for the walkers ever since was there large as life for the 50th. Hidden in the murky light of the Swan,Joan Goswell worked her usual miracle with the result sheets.…
Once again Jack and Joan Goswell worked miracles with the results, thanks to Bill Ashford whose kitchen is much preferred to the public bar of the Swan as the Open '7' Administrative HQ.
This election honours the Club as well as the individual; and in this connection we acknowledge with grateful thanks the additional hard work and support given by Mrs.

Jack Goswell as Master of Ceremonies, in all matters concerned with recording and producing results, ably abetted by his wife Joan. Although no one is indispensable, their absolutely unique service in producing complete duplicated results to all competitors must surely be irreplaceable.

A day spent with Jack and Joan Goswell, the company of our walkers, the knowledge that Belgrave had played its full part, administratively and in active participation, adds up to one thing - complete satisfaction.

We had a team of five in this ever popular walk, with Jack and Joan Goswell responsible for compiling the results. In the rush for the first mile Carl Lawton kept slightly behind the leading bunch, then on reaching the open road challenged for the lead to draw steadily away to win by 24 seconds.

Bill was just about to sign when the lad's father bellowed from the crowd, "No, not him, one of the others!" It was good to see JOAN GOSWELL at a recent fixture. A deterioration in her vision resulted in a visit to hospital and an operation.

The locals always appreciate the help they get from London and this popular fixture is always a 'must' for Jack and Joan Goswell who look after the results, ably assisted by Harry Shields who also judges.

However a number of Belgravians were on the Officials List, and looking at the programme we find Fred Denny (Recorder) Jack and Joan Goswell (Results) John Keown (Judges Recorder) Ray Middleton (Chief Steward Refreshment Station) and Jean Middleton (Sales and Programmes).
Generally it proved successful and once again thanks are due to those within the Belgrave circle but not actually members: Joan Goswell, Wyn Cook and Jean Middleton, who do such sterling work.

Jack Goswell keeps busy by running the Supporters Club Football Competition and is a Walking Judge and with the help of his wife Joan continue to produce those excellent result sheets after Walking events.

We drew blanks in the raffle but we must not grumble and maybe just as well judging by Carl's well laden van, trophies, grub and competitors etc. Yet again another well organised event and of course Jack and Joan Goswell were in on producing the results.
Once again, Jack and Joan Goswell produced their immaculate result sheet which showed 110 starters and 15 teams. Finally our thanks to Carl under whose guidance the race went without a hitch.
Results, of course, by Jack and Joan Goswell whose ability to produce the results so quickly is the envy of many. Behind the tea counter Brian Gorman and his small band of assistants.
The officials, timekeepers, pointsmen (we could do with more of those) recorders, judges and of course Jack and Joan Goswell, and the others I have forgotten, AND those that donate to the prize fund.
